title: F172 - Genetic Engineering: Lessons 9–12 (Gene Therapy, AMT-130 Clinical Trials & NEA Task 2)
courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology - Unit F172: Genetics
focus: Gene Therapy Delivery Vectors, AMT-130 Huntington's Disease Clinical Trial, Genetic Engineering vs Gene Therapy, CRISPR-Cas9, and NEA Task 2 Marking Rubrics (Pass, Merit, Distinction)
deliverable: Comprehensive slide deck and pedagogical resource covering Scheme of Work Lessons 9 to 12. Prepares learners for NEA Task 2 by rigorously addressing viral and non-viral vectors, clinical trial architecture, uniQure AMT-130 striatal microinfusion data (CSF mHTT, NfL, cUHDRS), somatic vs germline boundaries, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, and full alignment to Pass (P5, P7, P8), Merit (M3, M4, M5), and Distinction (D3, D4, D5) criteria.

objectives.knowledge: Explain the biological mechanisms of viral vectors (AAV5, Lentivirus, Adenovirus) and non-viral delivery platforms (LNPs, CED microinfusion, electroporation), distinguishing genetic engineering from somatic/germline gene therapy.
objectives.application: Analyze clinical trial phases (I, II, III) and evaluate the AMT-130 Huntington's disease clinical trial as an in situ AAV5-miRNA striatal gene silencing paradigm.
objectives.evaluation: Evaluate therapeutic outcomes, delivery challenges, and the role of genetic counselling against OCR AAQ Unit F172 NEA Task 2 assessment criteria across Pass, Merit, and Distinction levels.

terminology.def: A non-pathogenic, replication-deficient parvovirus vector with high neuronal tropism, maintaining episomal expression without host chromosomal integration.
An investigational gene therapy for Huntington's disease using an AAV5 vector to deliver a microRNA (miRNA) that binds to and degrades mutant HTT mRNA, lowering toxic huntingtin protein.
A neurosurgical infusion technique using a continuous positive-pressure gradient to drive macromolecular vectors through the brain parenchymal extracellular matrix.
An RNA-guided endonuclease system comprising a single guide RNA (sgRNA) complementary to a genomic target and Cas9 enzyme that induces a double-strand break adjacent to a 5'-NGG PAM motif.
Somatic therapy alters non-reproductive cells with non-heritable effects; germline alters gametes or early zygotes with permanent, heritable changes (strictly prohibited under UK HFEA regulations).

slides.title: Lesson 9 | Viral Vectors in Gene Therapy
slides.subtitle: Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV), Lentiviral, and Adenoviral delivery systems
keyTakeaways: AAV vectors exhibit high neuronal tropism and persist episomally, with a 4.7 kb packaging limit.
Lentiviral vectors integrate into host genomes for dividing lineages, accommodating up to 8-10 kb.
Adenoviral vectors provide high transient expression but provoke strong innate immune clearance.

Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV), Lentiviral, and Adenoviral delivery systems

slides.title: Lesson 9 | Non-Viral Vectors & Cellular Delivery Mechanisms
slides.subtitle: Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs) and Physical Delivery Modalities
keyTakeaways: Lipid Nanoparticles encapsulate nucleic acids and facilitate endosomal escape with minimal immunogenicity.
Physical modalities include electroporation and MRI-guided Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) for direct CNS infusion.

slides.title: Lesson 10 | Clinical Trial Architecture & The NEA Task 2 Framework
slides.subtitle: Phases I–III Clinical Trials and NEA Task 2 Assessment Rubric (P5, M3)
keyTakeaways: Phase I evaluates safety and dose escalation; Phase II tests biomarker proof-of-concept; Phase III runs double-blind RCTs.
NEA Task 2 requires describing at least two therapies (Pass P5) and deepening therapeutic context (Merit M3).

slides.title: Lesson 10 | Mapping Gene Delivery Strategies
slides.subtitle: Ex Vivo (In Vitro), In Vivo, and In Situ therapeutic routes
keyTakeaways: Ex vivo modifies autologous cells outside the body (CAR-T, HSCs).
In vivo administers vectors systemically (IV), requiring immune evasion.
In situ directly microinjects into localized tissues (e.g., striatum or retina).

slides.title: Lesson 10 | Cellular Targets & Genetic Counselling
slides.subtitle: Somatic vs Germline and Patient Support NEA Criteria (P8, M5)
keyTakeaways: Somatic therapy alters differentiated cells non-heritably; germline therapy alters gametes and is legally prohibited.
Genetic counsellors clarify inheritance risks, treatment viability, and psychological preparedness (P8, M5).

slides.title: Lesson 11 | Defining the Boundaries: Engineering vs. Therapy
slides.subtitle: Contrasting broad genetic engineering with targeted human gene therapy
keyTakeaways: Genetic engineering encompasses recombinant DNA applications across species (GMOs, biomanufacturing).
Gene therapy is strictly clinical, restoring normal human physiology without trait enhancement.

slides.title: Lesson 12 | CRISPR-Cas9: The Molecular Scalpel
slides.subtitle: Guide RNA targeting, Cas9 endonuclease cleavage, and NHEJ vs HDR repair
keyTakeaways: sgRNA guides Cas9 to genomic loci matching PAM (5'-NGG-3') sequence for double-strand break cleavage.
Repair pathways: error-prone NHEJ knocks out faulty genes; HDR introduces precise template-directed gene corrections.

slides.title: Lesson 12 | Evaluating CRISPR in a Clinical Context
slides.subtitle: Clinical Potential, Off-target Challenges, and Distinction Rubric (D3, D4, D5)
keyTakeaways: Offers curative potential for monogenic diseases like Sickle Cell Disease alongside multiplexing capability.
Requires critical evaluation against Distinction criteria: therapy relevance (D3) and multi-option appraisal (D4/D5).

slides.title: Lessons 9-12 | NEA Task 2 Master Synthesis
slides.subtitle: Graded roadmap for Pass, Merit, and Distinction achievement in Genetics NEA
keyTakeaways: Step 1: Pass Criteria (P5, P7, P8) - Research 2 therapies, explain delivery methods, and summarize counselling.
Step 2: Merit Criteria (M3, M4, M5) - Deepen therapeutic context, analyse delivery hurdles, and evaluate counselling benefits.
Step 3: Distinction Criteria (D3, D4, D5) - Critically discuss therapy relevance and assess three distinct holistic care options.
